summary.en: Salvadoran forces have launched missiles and ground attacks on Haitian gang hideouts, destroying the headquarters of the 400-member Mawozo gang and killing about 20 gang members. Haitian gang leader Mathias Saintil was killed in the strikes, and the Salvadoran president warned remaining gang leaders of further action. Haitian officials are traveling to El Salvador to discuss the future of the Salvadoran offensive, while Amnesty International has called for transparency on the deployment terms. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske styrker har skutt missiler og gjennomført bakkearrangementer mot haitiske gjengskjul, og har ødelagt hovedkvarteret til 400‑medlemers Mawozo-gjeng og drept omtrent 20 gjengmedlemmer. Den haitiske gjenglederen Mathias Saintil ble drept i angrepene, og den salvadoranske presidenten advarte gjenværende gjengledere om ytterligere handling. Haitiske tjenestemenn reiser til El Salvador for å diskutere fremtiden for den salvadoranske offensiven, mens Amnesty International har krevd åpenhet om vilkårene for utplasseringen. Konflikten førte til 193 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
